clue.text: The coach in bygone days

parts.note: a coach is a tutor, and bygone days are the past, so this is the teacher of the past as a school subject rather than an old stagecoach

explanation.surface: A nostalgic look at the horse-drawn coach of long ago.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Coach' suggests a carriage and 'bygone days' an old era; read instead as the schoolteacher whose subject is bygone days.
explanation.definitionFit: A coach is a tutor, and the past is the subject this school teacher covers.

clue.text: The worker getting behind isn't troubled for a moment

indicators.note: the worker's letters get behind, i.e. follow, the jumbled letters
troubled means disturbed or stirred up, so the letters of isn't are jumbled

parts.note: an ant is the classic crossword worker insect

explanation.surface: An employee falling behind who stays unbothered, if only briefly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'getting behind' sounds like falling behind schedule; it simply places the worker after the jumbled letters made by 'troubled'.
explanation.definitionFit: An instant is a very brief stretch of time, a split second.

clue.text: This should catch some reflection

indicators.note: a reflection shows things mirrored, so the word for some is read backwards

parts.note: some means a part or portion of something

explanation.surface: A remark about a mirror or window picking up a reflection.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reflection' turns PART round to give the snare.
explanation.definitionFit: A snare is a device built for catching animals.

clue.text: Quite unusual rose-red screen

indicators.note: something quite unusual is out of the ordinary, so the letters of rose-red are put in an odd order

explanation.surface: Admiring an uncommon pinkish-red room divider.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Quite unusual' rearranges ROSERED.
explanation.definitionFit: A reredos is an ornamental partition behind a church altar, a kind of carved screen.

clue.text: The accountants in the film calculated incorrectly

indicators.note: in places the accountants inside the word for film

parts.note: a film is a thin layer, as is a mist on glass
CA stands for chartered accountant, so CAs are accountants

explanation.surface: Accountants appear in a movie and botch the sums.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Film' suggests cinema, and the answer's usual sense (an actor wrongly chosen) fits that, but here to cast is the old bookkeeping verb for adding up.
explanation.definitionFit: To cast figures is an old term for adding them up, so to get the sum wrong is to do that badly.

clue.text: Boxes or trays for containing type

indicators.note: the words boxes or trays are said to contain the letters that make the answer

explanation.surface: Storage boxes or trays for holding printing type.
explanation.walkthrough: The run sits across the end of 'Boxes', 'or' and the start of 'trays'.
explanation.definitionFit: A sort is a kind or category, the same as a type.

clue.text: Directions to keep standard material for the paper

indicators.note: the outer letters hold or keep the word for standard within them

parts.note: E and S are compass directions, east and south
taken as written
par is the standard or normal level

explanation.surface: Instructions on keeping to the usual material used for making paper.
explanation.walkthrough: Esparto grass is used in making high-quality paper; 'to keep' has the outer pieces holding the golf standard.
explanation.definitionFit: Esparto is a tough grass used in making fine paper.

clue.text: Exciting tours made even hazardous

indicators.note: hazardous means risky or chancy, so the letters are thrown about into a new order

explanation.surface: Excursions turned even riskier for thrill-seekers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hazardous' rearranges TOURSMADEEVEN.
explanation.definitionFit: Something adventuresome is daring and thrilling, so it is stirring.

clue.text: The bicycle provided for coppers at one time

parts.note: the penny was an old British copper coin
the farthing, a quarter of a penny, was another old British copper coin, withdrawn in 1960

explanation.surface: A bicycle supplied for police officers in the past.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Coppers' suggests police; here it means copper coins. The Victorian bicycle with one huge and one tiny wheel was named after the large and small coins.
explanation.definitionFit: The high-wheeled Victorian cycle took its name from the contrast of a big coin with a little one.

clue.text: Feel most unhappy when praised in the wrong way

indicators.note: the letters of praised are put in the wrong way, i.e. in a scrambled order

explanation.surface: Being miserable at receiving clumsy praise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in the wrong way' rearranges PRAISED.
explanation.definitionFit: To despair is to lose all hope, to be utterly miserable.

clue.text: A light-weight has reason to hesitate

explanation.surface: A lightweight boxer has cause to hold back.
explanation.definitionFit: A scruple is an old apothecaries' unit of twenty grains, a tiny weight, and also a moral doubt that makes one hold back.

clue.text: Some wanted American cheese

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Some people wanted an American cheese.
explanation.walkthrough: The run straddles 'wantED AMerican'; the cheese is Dutch, not American.
explanation.definitionFit: Edam is a mild Dutch cheese with a red wax rind.

clue.text: One trade setting a very high standard

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
a deal is a trade or transaction

explanation.surface: A single business agreement setting an impressive benchmark.
explanation.definitionFit: An ideal is a standard of perfection to aim for.

clue.text: None hurried to make port

parts.note: O, as zero, means none
ran means hurried

explanation.surface: Nobody rushed to reach the harbour.
explanation.walkthrough: Oran is a port city in Algeria.
explanation.definitionFit: Oran is a Mediterranean harbour city in Algeria.

clue.text: A number may be looked at about five

indicators.note: the word for looked at goes about, i.e. around, the numeral

parts.note: seen is how something looked at may be described
V is the Roman numeral for five

explanation.surface: A figure might be examined around the number five.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts V inside SEEN.
explanation.definitionFit: Seven is a whole number, one more than six.

clue.text: Heavens above!

parts.note: looks like an exclamation of surprise but is read literally as the heavens that are above us

explanation.surface: An exclamation of astonishment.
explanation.definitionFit: The heavens are the vault overhead, the firmament.

clue.text: Staggers the salvage-collectors

explanation.surface: The scrap merchants are reeling.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain a totter is a rag-and-bone man who goes round collecting scrap and junk.
explanation.definitionFit: To totter is to stagger unsteadily, and totters in British slang are rag-and-bone men collecting scrap.

clue.text: Drop parody

explanation.surface: Abandon the spoof.
explanation.definitionFit: To take off can mean to remove or deduct, as in dropping an item, and a take-off is a mocking imitation.

clue.text: Check a note on newspapers

parts.note: re is a note of the sol-fa scale
the press means newspapers collectively

explanation.surface: Glance at a memo about the papers.
explanation.definitionFit: To repress is to hold back or restrain, i.e. to keep in check.

clue.text: Restrained and content like a country person

indicators.note: the content of the word for restrained, what it holds inside, is the phrase like a

parts.note: pent, as in pent-up, means held back
as means like

explanation.surface: Calm and satisfied, as a rural dweller supposedly is.
explanation.walkthrough: 'content' looks like an adjective meaning satisfied; read as a noun, the contents, it says what sits inside the word for restrained.
explanation.definitionFit: A peasant is a small farmer or farm labourer living in the countryside.

clue.text: No thugs used a firearm

indicators.note: used here means put to work in a new form, so the letters of no thugs are rearranged

explanation.surface: No gangsters fired a weapon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'used' rearranges NOTHUGS.
explanation.definitionFit: A shotgun is a smooth-bore gun firing pellets, a type of gun.

clue.text: Being less encumbered, the French are in credit

indicators.note: in places the French article and are inside the credit abbreviation

parts.note: CR is the accounting abbreviation for credit
le is French for the
taken as written

explanation.surface: The French are financially in the black and so less burdened.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' places the French article and the verb inside the accounting abbreviation, splitting it.
explanation.definitionFit: Less obstructed or freer of clutter, comparative of free of obstacles.

clue.text: Greek character set against alcoholic drink

parts.note: chi is a letter of the Greek alphabet
anti means against

explanation.surface: A Greek person is firmly opposed to drinking.
explanation.definitionFit: Chianti is a red wine from Tuscany.

clue.text: Regret holding vital material back, and withdraw

indicators.note: the word for regret holds the reversed letters within it

parts.note: to rue is to regret

indicators.note: back means the word for vital material is read in reverse

parts.note: a gene is the basic material of heredity in living things

explanation.surface: Feel sorry about keeping essential supplies back, and pull out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns the hereditary unit round (ENEG); 'holding' wraps the word for regret around it. Renegue is a variant spelling of renege.
explanation.definitionFit: To renegue is to go back on a promise, backing out of it.

clue.text: A biscuit for break?

explanation.surface: A cookie for a rest period?
explanation.definitionFit: A snap is a crisp thin biscuit, as in ginger snap, and to snap is to break suddenly.

clue.text: A jerk without work is the subject of discussion

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the word for jerk sits outside the word for work

parts.note: a tic is an involuntary twitch or jerk
op, short for opus, is a work

explanation.surface: An idler who won't work is what everyone talks about.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' means outside here, not lacking: an old sense still common in crosswords.
explanation.definitionFit: A topic is a theme or matter being talked about.

clue.text: Every a king.' Shakespeare (King Lear)

parts.note: a fill-in-the-blank quotation: Lear's line has one word missing between every and a king

explanation.surface: A line from King Lear with a word left out.
explanation.walkthrough: Lear's line is the missing word between 'Every' and 'a king'; it means wholly or in every part.
explanation.definitionFit: The missing word is a small unit of length, and the phrase means a king through and through.

clue.text: Yarn connecting an army man with a politician

parts.note: GI is an American soldier
MP stands for Member of Parliament

explanation.surface: A tale linking a soldier with a member of parliament.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Yarn' suggests a story; here it is thread.
explanation.definitionFit: Gimp is a twisted silk or cotton thread used in trimming and lace.

clue.text: A knot tier stood up

indicators.note: in a down clue stood up means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: a rank is a tier or level

explanation.surface: Someone tying a knot was left waiting by a date.
explanation.walkthrough: 'knot tier' suggests someone tying knots; split it, 'A knot' is the definition and 'tier' the rank.
explanation.definitionFit: A knar is a knot or gnarl in wood.

clue.text: Sense men gain by making changes

indicators.note: changes to the letters of men gain shuffle them into a new order

explanation.surface: Men become wiser by altering their ways.
explanation.walkthrough: 'by making changes' rearranges MENGAIN.
explanation.definitionFit: Meaning is the sense or significance of something.

clue.text: Figure the hack will appear in time

indicators.note: the horse will appear inside the word for time

parts.note: noon is a time of day
a hack is a riding horse, as is a nag

explanation.surface: A journalist will turn up on time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hack' suggests a journalist; it is a horse. 'will appear in' sets it inside the midday time.
explanation.definitionFit: A nonagon is a geometric shape with nine sides.

clue.text: Judges it's mad to keep personal records

indicators.note: mad means crazy, so the letters of it's are scrambled

parts.note: to pen is to keep shut in, as animals in an enclosure
diaries are personal daily records

explanation.surface: It's crazy to hold on to private journals.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mad' rearranges ITS to STI. Stipendiaries are paid magistrates in Britain, as opposed to unpaid lay magistrates.
explanation.definitionFit: Stipendiary magistrates are salaried legal officials who sit in judgment.
